errors.description: Model incorrectly assigned colors to cube faces, claiming red faces are hidden on the left and middle cubes when ground truth shows no red faces are hidden on any cube.
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: 'Left Cube: ... The Red face must be hidden... Hidden red faces: 1.' 'Middle Cube: ... The Red face is not visible... Hidden red faces: 1.'

errors.description: Model associated the color red with hidden faces on cubes where red was either not present or visible, misassigning the attribute 'red' to incorrect spatial positions.
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: 'Right Cube: ... Red (front) ... Hidden red faces: 0.' — correctly identifies visible red, but incorrectly infers red must be hidden on other cubes despite no evidence.

errors.description: Model assumed each cube must have a red face and that it must be hidden if not visible, violating the ground truth which explicitly lists all face colors per cube — including that Cube 3 has only one red face (on the bottom, which is hidden, but model misassigned it as front).
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: '...assuming the cube is colored with one red face, the red face is not visible...' — this assumption is unsupported and contradicts provided face color data.

analysis_result.analysis: The model’s reasoning is fundamentally flawed due to incorrect perception of face colors and faulty assumptions about cube coloring. It hallucinated red faces on cubes where none exist in the hidden positions (as per ground truth) and misassigned the single red face (on Cube 3’s bottom) as visible (front). This cascades into an incorrect total of 2 hidden red faces instead of 0. The error stems from ignoring the explicit face-color mapping provided in the ground truth and instead inferring colors based on visibility alone, which violates the problem’s constraints.
